_doc: GOAL-ZERO-ENTER-DAYS-2026-09-03 Z6 -- 10-30 checkpoint prereg for the gate the Z1-Z5 backfill most frequently indicts. FROZEN BEFORE ANY RESULT. This file proposes NOTHING for the live config now (CONFIG FREEZE 2026-08-31 -> 2026-10-30) -- it registers the question, the population, and the analysis method in advance of the 10-30 checkpoint, per the goal's OPERATING RULES.
label: F10-VOL-BASELINE-SESSION-RESET

gate_indicted.function: buyer_pressure_bar_v11 (backtest/lib/filters.py) -- green-bar + volume >= f10_vol_mult * vol_baseline_20 check, f10_vol_mult=0.7
gate_indicted.mechanism_under_question: vol_baseline_20bar computes a 20-bar trailing SMA of volume over a CONTINUOUS, RTH-only, multi-day series with NO per-day reset (backtest/lib/filters.py:131-135, mirrored at setup/scripts/heartbeat_core.py:928) -- for the first ~20 RTH bars of any trading day (09:35-~11:15 ET) the lookback reaches into the PRIOR day's RTH tail. Candidate change (NOT proposed for shipping now): reset the 20-bar baseline at each session open instead of carrying it across days.

why_this_gate_and_not_blocker_8.blocker_8_note: Filter 8 (VIX floor, mirrored bull/bear forms) was the DOMINANT (first-listed) blocker on 3 of 5 backfilled days (2026-08-31, 09-01, 09-04 -- all BEAR-thesis days, 64-77 bars each). It is EXCLUDED from this prereg to avoid duplicating existing coverage: the bear-side VIX floor already has a live, dated prereg + accruing shadow ledger -- analysis/recommendations/VIX-FLOOR-SHADOW-PREREG-2026-08-27.md, vix-floor-shadow-ledger.jsonl, vix-floor-shadow-summary.json -- filed 2026-08-27, before this goal existed. Filing a second prereg for the same mechanism would violate the Obsidian-brain dedup rule (check for prior coverage before building; fold into the existing living doc, never a parallel one). New Z5 evidence on blocker 8 should be FOLDED into that existing prereg's evidence base by a follow-up fire, not duplicated here.
why_this_gate_and_not_blocker_8.blocker_10_note: Filter 10 (f10 volume/buyer-pressure) has NO existing prereg or shadow instrument (verified: analysis/recommendations/ has no f10/vol-baseline-specific prereg predating this one) and, measured by DIRECT MEMBERSHIP (blocker id present anywhere in the thesis side's blocker list for that bar -- the same method SIP-VOLMULT-2026-09-02.md and the Z2 hand-fill both used, not just 'first-listed'), fires on EVERY ONE of the 5 backfilled days at 50.6%-74.0% of bars -- a more consistent cross-day signal than blocker 8's day-level dominance count. This is also the SAME gate the goal's own SIP-VOLMULT-2026-09-02 research already flagged as 'a candidate for a 10-30 prereg, not before' -- this file executes that flag using the fuller 5-day backfill instead of the single day it was based on.

aggregated_evidence_from_z5_backfill.method: For each of the 5 in-scope days (analysis/zero-enter/ZERO-ENTER-INVENTORY-2026-09-03.json), count unique RTH 5-min bars (account=safe, dedup by trigger_bar_et, last occurrence kept -- SIP-VOLMULT-2026-09-02.md's own method) where blocker id 10 is present anywhere in the day's dominant-thesis-side blocker list.

per_day.note: n_bars=67 not 77 -- 2026-09-04 has a 09:51-10:46 ET power-outage gap (rows absent, not a gate); treated as NO_DATA, never misread as gated

question_for_10_30: Does resetting vol_baseline_20bar's 20-bar SMA at each RTH session open (instead of the current cross-day continuous trailing window) materially change (a) blocker-10's fire rate on the days it currently indicts, and (b) the OOS-validated PF/expectancy of the setups it would newly admit -- net of the same realistic cost model (backtest/lib/simulator_real.py slippage) this goal's own autopsy instrument uses? SIP-VOLMULT-2026-09-02.md's own sensitivity check (same-day-only baseline) showed SIP and IEX agree on 50/50 identical blocked bars once cross-session contamination is removed, vs 55-58/77 with it -- i.e. the session-reset change would ONLY affect ~5-8 bars/day (the session-crossing residual), not the bulk of the day's blocking (which is real low-turnover volume, not a computation artifact).
